newsitem.title: USA: Chico's FAS president on leave of absence.
newsitem.headline: Chico's FAS president on leave of absence.

text.p: Chico's FAS Inc said Tuesday that President Melissa Payner had taken a leave of absence while she and the company attempt to work out a separation agreement.

The company issued the announcement as it reported a net loss of some $747,000, or $0.09 per share, for its fourth quarter ended February 1. A year earlier the company lost about $137,000, or $0.02 per share.

Marvin Gralnick, chief executive, said that although Chico's FAS reported an increase in earnings for the full fiscal year, "the members of our senior management group have had a significant difference of views as to the strategic direction for the company's future."
For the 53 weeks ended February 1, earnings rose to $1.9 million, or $.24 per share, from $1.7 million, or $.21 per share, for the 52-week year ended January 28, 1996.
"Our inability to agree on direction has resulted in our working on the anticipated separation with Melissa," he said.

"However, while we are working through matters with Melissa, we feel it is best not to comment further concerning the anticipated separation," he said. The company expects to provide more details within the next few weeks, he said.
Charles Kleman, executive vice president, has taken over the role of providing the day-to-day direction for planning, buying and inventory management, he said.
Gralnick said he is guiding the company's team handling product development and production.

Selling, general and administrative expenses for the 14 weeks ended February 1 include the establishment of a reserve of about $200,000 after tax, or $0.02 per share, in order to address costs associated with the anticipated management change, the company said.

Chico's FAS sells exclusively designed, private-label women's casual clothing and related accessories. It operates a chain of 135 stores in 32 states; 126 stores are company-owned and nine are franchised.
